<action type="say">
Here are the Outlook-specific steps and a short note you can use.

OUTLOOK DESKTOP (Windows/Mac)
1) Open Outlook and go to Calendar.
2) Navigate to December 9, 2025.
3) Double‑click the “Research Sync” meeting where you’re the organizer.
4) In the meeting window:
   - Change only the **Date** field from **12/9/2025** to **12/10/2025**.
   - Leave the **Start time** and **End time** as they are (to keep the same one‑hour afternoon slot).
5) (Optional) In the meeting body, paste the short note to attendees (below).
6) Click **Send Update** so attendees receive the new date.

OUTLOOK ON THE WEB (Office 365 / Outlook.com)
1) Go to Outlook in your browser and open **Calendar**.
2) Jump to **December 9, 2025**.
3) Click the “Research Sync” meeting, then click **Edit** (or **Edit series** if it’s recurring and you’re moving only that instance, choose **Edit occurrence**).
4) In the edit pane:
   - Change the **date** from **Dec 9, 2025** to **Dec 10, 2025**.
   - Keep the start/end times the same.
5) (Optional) Paste the short note into the description/body.
6) Click **Send** or **Send update**.

SHORT NOTE TO ATTENDEES
You can paste this into the meeting body or send as an email:

Subject (if emailing): Research Sync – date change

Body:
Hi all,

Our “Research Sync” meeting originally scheduled for Tuesday, December 9, 2025 has been moved to Wednesday, December 10, 2025 at the same time. The agenda and format remain the same.

Please let me know if the new time causes any issues for you.

Best,  
Lisa

If you tell me your time zone (and the exact hour, e.g., 2–3 pm ET), I can double-check wording so it explicitly states the new time as well.</action>
